title: commitment-signals-for-cost-latency-aware-rollouts-wip
summary: Working notes for defining commitment signals used to gate and drive cross-functional canary and A/B rollouts where cost and latency trade-offs are first-class signals.
content:
Purpose
======
Quick working draft: define a compact set of "commitment signals" that product, infra, and SRE can use to make consistent decisions during canary/A-B rollouts where cost and latency are treated as primary inputs alongside quality metrics. Goal is operational clarity: what to watch, how often, and what actions to take when signals disagree.

Context and motivation
----------------------
- We frequently face rollouts where a model variant reduces cost (token spend) but increases p95 latency slightly, or vice-versa. Current runbooks emphasize errors and model quality; we lack a concise framing for explicit trade-offs and for automated/semiautomated commitments.
- This doc is intended for product PMs, rollout owners, infra (autoscaling/batching), and SRE to align on guardrails.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated rollouts. Private deployments: use as template but map signals to customer-specific telemetry.
- Focus on canaries and small-ratio A/B experiments (<=20% traffic). Not for full fleet migrations.

Commitment signal categories (short list)
----------------------------------------
1) User-facing latency (p50/p90/p95) — measured at route level and model variant level.
2) Cost-per-1k-tokens (effective unit cost) — includes infra amortized + direct model cost estimate.
3) Error/5xx rate and clear signal of correctness regressions (intent-level fuzzy matching).
4) Quality/semantic regressions — eval prompt-suite pass-rate delta (daily rolling).
5) Resource pressure signals — GPU queue length, OOMs, autoscaler thrashing.
6) Safety/hallucination proxies — hallucination classifier score aggregate, rate of customer escalations.

For each: definition, primary data source, preferred aggregation window, suggested alert threshold (initial).

Examples (defaults, starting point)
----------------------------------
- p95 latency: route-level 5m rolling median; alert if > baseline + 25% AND absolute > 500ms for 5 consecutive 5m windows.
- Cost/1k tokens: compute via billing-slice pipeline; alert if cost drop > 15% (positive) but any latency increase > 20% (conflict) — surface to owners, do not auto-promote.
- Error rate: 5xx increase > 50% relative to baseline AND absolute > 0.5% -> immediate rollback trigger.
- Eval pass-rate: drop > 4 percentage points on prioritized prompt set over 24h -> manual investigation required.
- GPU queue length: > 2x baseline for 10m -> throttle new canary traffic.

Decision policy primitives
-------------------------
- Safe Rollback: immediate automated rollback when critical safety or correctness thresholds hit (5xx, safety classifier spikes, OOM).
- Throttle: reduce canary traffic by factor (e.g., half) when resource signals or transient latency spikes detected.
- Pause: hold further increases in allocation / rollout for human review when quality vs cost trade-off is ambiguous.
- Promote: only after sustained window with all primary signals in green for at least 24h and no quality regression.

Conflict resolution rules (simple precedence)
-------------------------------------------
1) Safety/correctness (quality regressions, safety classifier, 5xx) outranks cost/latency benefits.
2) Resource saturation outranks cost signals (we cannot accept lower infra cost if it causes thrashing).
3) If cost is improved but latency worsened slightly (<15% relative) and quality is neutral, require explicit product sign-off (PM + infra).

Observation cadence and dashboards
---------------------------------
- Live (real-time) dashboard: p95/p90/p50, 5xx rate, GPU queue, cost per 1k tokens. 1m granularity for latency, 5m for others.
- Rolling windows for decisions: short-term (15m), medium (3h), sustained (24h). Promotion requires medium+ sustained windows.
- Suggested alerts: short noisy alerts to SRE; louder, ticketed alerts to rollout owner and PM when medium thresholds breached.

Rollback and mitigation profiles (templates)
-------------------------------------------
- Profile A (safety-critical): immediate auto-rollback. Triggers: safety classifier spike > 3x baseline; user escalations > 5 within 10m for canary slice.
- Profile B (resource): automated throttle -> if persists 30m escalate to SRE. Triggers: GPU queue > 2x baseline, OOMs.
- Profile C (cost/latency conflict): pause + human review. Triggers: cost decrease > 15% AND p95 increase > 20% relative.

Pre-launch checklist (owner-run)
-------------------------------
- Create experiment ticket + hypothesis (JIRA-ROLL-78 or similar).
- Define baseline windows and sampling slices (route ids, regions).
- Register commit signals and thresholds in rollout ticket.
- Wire dashboards and alerting; verify queries run against baseline data.
- Set experiment owner and on-call contact list.
- Prepare canary fallback model and routing policy (auto-fallback endpoint).

During-rollout checklist
------------------------
- Monitor short and medium windows; respond to alerts.
- Run daily eval suite against canary variant and baseline.
- Annotate decision log in the ticket whenever a throttle/pause/promotion occurs.
- Keep SRE and infra looped in for resource anomalies.

Post-rollout checklist
----------------------
- Summarize metrics, cost delta, latency delta, and quality deltas.
- Update runbook thresholds if signals were either too noisy or too sensitive.
- Capture lessons and update eval prompt sets if new failure modes observed.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- How do we normalize cost across Hosted vs Dedicated where billing models differ? (Action: Marco to prototype cost-normalizer, due 2025-03-18, JIRA-PR-399).
- Should small latency regressions for interactive endpoints be allowed if cost drops significantly for background inference? Need classification by endpoint criticality. (Action: Priya to propose classification matrix).
- Can we automate combined-signal scoring for auto-promote vs triage? Need ML/heuristics owner. (Action: Ben to scope POC).

Notes to self / operational hints
--------------------------------
- During high-noise periods (region maintenance, infra flapping) raise thresholds temporarily and annotate ticket, otherwise noisy rollouts lead to churn.
- Keep canary slices diverse (region + user agent + route) — avoids narrow-corner regressions.
- Track cost signal with sliding percentile (p50 of cost/1k tokens) rather than raw mean to avoid outlier bias.

References and links
--------------------
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/Canary+Playbook (work-in-progress)
- JIRA: JIRA-ROLL-78 (current experiment ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/342 (canary autoscaler tweaks)

If this provides value we should fold into the canonical rollout-runbook and add a short decision matrix UI in Console so PMs can pick premade "commitment profiles" (Profile A/B/C) when creating rollouts.

-- Aisha
